limits: These are single fuel droplets (methanol, heptane), not cabin materials. The tool supports fire-safety reasoning; it does not predict a cabin fire.
"Visible flame extinction" may not be the end of burning: FLEX found heptane droplets can keep burning in an invisible cool flame.
Suppressant is added at constant total pressure, replacing part of the O2/N2 mix, as in the NASA tests.
The burning-rate unit and the gas labels (O2, N2, CO2) are still unconfirmed: the NASA file header prints "mm" and "O", "N", "CO".
The NASA table does not separate space tests from ground tests.
note: mean, lower, upper and in_range are model.predict() output; the d_ext/d0 mean and interval are clipped to [0, 1] by predict(). crossing and sentence come from lab.curve() with step 0.005 over the tested range of the slice, as on the Streamlit Suppression Lab.
